headline: Approved two-year snow and ice removal contract for $54,360 per year and a painting and cleaning contract for vacant units.
summary: Commissioners discussed unpaid rent and housing waiting lists. They also received an update on the Maynard Homes Redevelopment Project, where work continues on four new buildings. The City opened a resource center at 45 High Street for people who are homeless, and a warming station is set to open November 15 at Elm Street School.
decisions: Approved the September 18, 2026 minutes; motion passed unanimously.
Approved the September 2026 monthly operational reports; motion passed unanimously.
Approved the Executive Director’s Report; motion passed unanimously.
Approved a two-year painting and cleaning contract for vacant units with All Around General Contracting and Plumbing, LLC, 5-0 roll call.
Approved a two-year snow and ice removal contract with Birch Hill Landscaping, LLC at $54,360 per year, 5-0 roll call.
Approved signature authority for Scott A. Costa and appointed Deanna Brooks as Authority secretary, 5-0 roll call.
Approved payment of bills from check numbers 73779 through 73884 and Park View check numbers 6083 through 6085; motion passed unanimously.
Recommended that the Board of Commissioners’ positions remain the same for the next two years.

plain_text:
MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING 
OF THE COMMISSIONERS OF THE 
NASHUA HOUSING AND REDEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY 
HELD ON OCTOBER 16, 2026 
 
 The Commissioners of the Nashua Housing  and Redevelopment Authority (NHRA) held 
its regular meeting at the office of the Nashua Housing and Redevelopment Authority, 40 East 
Pearl Street, Nashua, New Hampshire, at 8:30 a.m. on Friday, October 16, 2026. Chairperson 
Eric Wilson  called the meeting to order, and the Recording Secretary called the roll at 
approximately 8:33 a.m. with the following responses: 
   
Present Absent 
Eric Wilson  
Paul Deschenes  
Helen Honorow  
Thomas Monahan  
James Tollner  
  
 The following persons were also present: Bob Mack, Director, City of Nashua  Welfare 
Department; Tonia Knisley, Voices of Major Drive ; Lori Wilshire , President , Board of 
Aldermen; Bob Keating, Granite State Organizing Project; Victoria Markiewicz, Granite State 
Organizing Project;  Phillip Mann, Resident ; Joseph Plodzik, Resident; Jessica Connors , 
Public Health Housing Services Officer; William Ayer III, Resident; Lynn Lombardi, Executive 
Director, and Deanna Brooks, Recording Secretary.  
 
MINUTES: 
 
 The Chairperson entertained a motion to waive the reading of the Authority’s regular 
meeting minutes dated September 18, 2026 , accept them, and place them on file.  Mr. 
Deschenes made a motion, and Ms. Honorow seconded the motion. The Chairperson asked 
if there were any comments, additions/deletions, corrections, or discussion. 
 
 There being no further discussion, the motion passed unanimously. 
 
 
 
 
DRAFT
COMMUNICATIONS: 
 
 The Chairperson entertained a motion to waive the reading of the Communications, accept 
them, and place them on file. Mr. Monahan made a motion  to accept, and Mr. Deschenes 
seconded the motion. The Communications were as follows:  Monthly Operational Reports – 
September 2026 – consisting of the Public Housing and Section 8 Waiting List and 
Applications Report; Work Order Report; Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher Program (HCVP) 
Utilization Report and Rent Collections Report. 
 
 The Chairperson asked if there were any comments or discussion. 
 
 Mr. Deschenes inquired about the rent receivables and expressed concerns regarding the 
high percentage of rents owed.  Ms. Lombardi explained that this often occurs within smaller 
developments and noted that the NHRA is awaiting payments from external assistance 
sources, including an out-of-state agency. She added that she is currently working with the 
attorney to file eviction actions in court.   
 
 Mr. Monahan asked whether the rent receivable amount includes last month's write -off. 
Ms. Lombardi confirmed it does not.  
 
 Mr. Monahan reported that the current total number of applicants on the waiting lists is 
4,348 for Public Housing, 5,451 for Section 8 HCV, 536 for Cotton Mill PBV, 374 for Salmon 
Brook, and 1,306 for Monahan Manor. He stated that the NHRA is doing a great job and noted 
that continued improvement is needed.  
 
 The Chairperson asked if there were any additional comments or discussion. There being 
none, the motion passed unanimously.  
 
EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR’S REPORT: 
 
 For the Maynard Homes Redevelopment Project, work continues across all four new 
buildings and the site. In Building #1, work continues on the third -floor walls and framing of 
both stairwells. In Building #3, wall framing began on September 28, while wall framing at 
Building #4 was scheduled to begin on October 5. In Building #2, trunk line installation has 
begun, with the north side nearly complete, and the electrical underground installation is 
ongoing. Installation of light pole bases, drainage, and structures is  in progress. Trailhead 
gravel is complete, with only the fencing remaining. 
DRAFT
We have been invited to meet with Sean W. Thomas, New Hampshire State Director for the 
U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) in Manchester, to discuss the 
work of the Nashua Housing and Redevelopment Authority and opportunities for collaboration. 
The visit will provide an opportunity to highlight our current initiatives, share our priorities and 
challenges, and discuss ways to strengthen our partnership with HUD in support of affordable 
housing and the residents we serve. 
The meeting will also allow us to learn more about HUD’s priorities for New Hampshire and 
explore opportunities to advance our mission and support the continued housing needs of the 
Nashua community. The participation of Mr. Wilson and an additional Commissioner is 
welcome. The meeting is tentatively scheduled for October 29, 2026, with the time yet to be 
confirmed. Additional details will be shared once the meeting time is finalized. 
 
 The Chairperson entertained a motion to approve the Executive Director’s Re port. Mr. 
Monahan made a motion, and Mr. Deschenes seconded the motion. The Chairperson asked 
if there were any comments or discussion. 
 
 Mr. Deschenes sought clarification on the location of the meeting. Ms. Lombardi confirmed 
it would be held at the Main Office, 40 East Pearl Street. 
 
 Mr. Monahan asked whether the radiant heat pumps discussed at last month's meeting 
are still in progress and requested that the NHRA  continue monitoring the process . Ms. 
Lombardi confirmed that the program is ongoing and will continue to be monitored. 
  
  There being no further discussion, the motion passed unanimously.  
 
NEW BUSINESS: 
 
RESOLUTION NO. 26-2515 
BY THE NASHUA HOUSING AND REDEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY 
AWARDING A TWO-YEAR CONTRACT BEGINNING NOVEMBER 1, 2026 AND ENDING 
OCTOBER 31, 2028 FOR PAINTING AND CLEANING OF VACANT UNITS TO ALL 
AROUND GENERAL CONTRACTING AND PLUMBING, LLC,  
49A STREET, MANCHESTER, NH 03102 AT A PER-UNIT COST AS OUTLINED 
 ON ATTACHED NARRATIVE UNDER THE OPERATING BUDGET 
 
 The Chairperson entertained a motion to approve Resolution No. 26-2515. Mr. Monahan 
made a motion, and M r. Tollner seconded the motion. The Chairperson asked if there were 
any comments or discussion. 
 
DRAFT
Mr. Wilson noted that the bid prices were close and asked whether the NHRA had 
previously used the contractor. Ms. Lombardi stated that the NHRA has used the contractor 
for general contracting services and is satisfied with the quality of their work. 
 There being no further discussion, the Recording Secretary called the roll with the 
following responses: 
 
AYE NAY 
James Tollner  
Thomas Monahan  
Helen Honorow  
Paul Deschenes  
Eric Wilson  
 
RESOLUTION NO. 26-2516 
BY THE NASHUA HOUSING AND REDEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY 
AWARDING A TWO-YEAR CONTRACT BEGINNING NOVEMBER 1, 2026,  
AND ENDING OCTOBER 31, 2028 FOR SNOW AND ICE REMOVAL SERVICES TO  
BIRCH HILL LANDSCAPING, LLC, 36 NEW DUNSTABLE ROAD, NASHUA, NH 03063 
AT A TOTAL CONTRACT COST OF $54,360 PER YEAR ($52,260 UNDER THE 
OPERATING BUDGET AND $2,100 UNDER THE 
 PARK VIEW APARTMENTS BUDGET) 
 
 The Chairperson entertained a motion to approve Resolution No. 26-2516. Mr. Monahan 
made a motion, and M r. Deschenes seconded the motion. The Chairperson asked if there 
were any comments or discussion. 
   
 Mr. Monahan expressed satisfaction with the bid price for this service. 
 
 Mr. Deschenes drew attention to the bid tabulation, noting that there was no check mark 
indicating insurance was provided , and ask ed whether the  contractor submitted it. Ms. 
Lombardi explained that Birch Hill Landscaping is the NHRA’s current contractor and that the 
Authority already has their insurance information on file. 
 
 There being no further discussion, the Recording Secretary called the roll with the 
following responses: 
 
DRAFT
AYE NAY 
James Tollner  
Thomas Monahan  
Helen Honorow  
Paul Deschenes  
Eric Wilson  
 
RESOLUTION NO. 26-2517 
BY THE NASHUA HOUSING AND REDEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY 
AUTHORIZING SIGNATURE AUTHORITY TO SCOTT A. COSTA,  
ASSISTANT EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR, AND APPOINTING  
DEANNA BROOKS, EXECUTIVE SECRETARY, AS SECRETARY  
FOR THE AUTHORITY 
 
 The Chairperson entertained a motion to approve Resolution No. 26-2517. Mr. Monahan 
made a motion, and M r. Deschenes seconded the motion. The Chairperson asked if there 
were any comments or discussion. 
 
 Mr. Monahan commented that the resolution is very appropriate and stated that he is in 
favor of it.   
 
 There being no further discussion, the Recording Secretary called the roll with the 
following responses: 
 
AYE NAY 
James Tollner  
Thomas Monahan  
Helen Honorow  
Paul Deschenes  
Eric Wilson  
  
BILLS/INVESTMENTS: 
 
 The Chairperson called for a motion to pay the bills as listed on the Cash Disbursement 
List - check numbers 73 779 through 73 884 and from the Park View Apartments Cash 
Disbursement List - check numbers 6083 through 6085, including ACH debits and investment 
accounts. Mr. Monahan made a motion, and Mr. Deschenes seconded. 
DRAFT
The Chairperson asked if there were any comments or discussion. 
 
 Ms. Lombardi explained that the Maynard Homes Redevelopment payments are fully 
reimbursable to the NHRA through the Authority’s  lenders and noted that the NHRA is  
currently working toward a closing date for the Phase II Predevelopment fund s with the 
Genesis Community Loan Fund. 
 
 Mr. Tollner asked about check number 73799 and requested that the NHRA monitor the 
investment rates, as rates are increasing broadly. Ms. Lombardi clarified that payment reflects 
reimbursement to Tremont Development, which  covered the initial upfront costs for solar 
consultation. She added that  she will  ask the finance department to review the current 
investment rates. 
 
 There being no further discussion, the motion passed unanimously. 
 
COMMISSIONER’S COMMENTS: 
 
 Mr. Monahan commended North Branch Construction for an excellent job on the 
redevelopment project and for maintaining a sanitary, safe environment for residents.   
 
 Mr. Deschenes commented that no Resident Advisory Board ( RAB) meeting has been 
held yet. Ms. Lombardi stated she is working with Mr. Costa to finalize the Five-Year CFP 
Plan and Annual Public Housing Plan and will reach out once they are complete. 
 
 Mr. Tollner recommended that the Board of Commissioners’ positions remain the same 
for the next two years.  
 
 Mr. Monahan agreed. 
  
ANY OTHER BUSINESS THAT MAY COME BEFORE THE BOARD: 
 
 None. 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT: 
 
 Mr. Mann asked about the status of hiring a Property Manager and expressed concerns 
regarding illegal activity occurring on the property . Ms. Lombardi asked him to contact the 
DRAFT
Assistant Property Manager, Tony Lozado , and encouraged him to continue reporting 
concerns to the NHRA. 
 
 Mr. Mack noted that the City of Nashua recently opened a resource center at 45 High 
Street, Nashua, NH, to assist the homeless population and provide other opportunities for 
individuals seeking to connect with community health workers.  He stated that the Continuum 
of Care program (CoC) has submitted its funding application and hopes that the necessary 
funding will continue to be available. 
 
 Mr. Tollner asked Mr. Mack to share information about the newly opened resource center 
with downtown businesses, noting that several he spoke with were not aware of the details. 
 
 Mr. Mack stated that the information had previously been shared, though attendance was 
limited, and he will make additional outreach efforts. Ms. Connors agreed to assist and noted 
that a press release is forthcoming. 
 
 Mr. Tollner asked Mr. Mack about the status of the warming station. Mr. Mack confirmed 
that the target opening date is November 15th, and that it will continue to operate at the fold 
Elm Street School. 
 
ADJOURNMENT: 
 
 The Chairperson entertained a motion to adjourn. Mr. Deschenes moved to adjourn, and 
Ms. Honorow seconded the motion.  
 
 There being no further discussion, the motion passed unanimously.  
 
 The meeting adjourned at approximately 9:01 a.m. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
 
Deanna Brooks 
Recording Secretary
